questions.prompt: Organic chemistry is the study of ____-based compounds.
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon-based compounds, which are fundamental to life.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and ____.
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon is a compound that contains carbon and hydrogen only.

questions.prompt: The three hydrocarbon families are alkanes, alkenes and ____.
questions.explanation: The hydrocarbon families are alkanes (C–C single bonds), alkenes (C=C) and alkynes (C≡C).

questions.prompt: A ____ group is an atom or group of atoms that classifies an organic compound into a class.
questions.explanation: All compounds with the same functional group belong to the same class.

questions.prompt: The functional group present in alcohols is the ____ group.
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group –OH.

questions.prompt: The functional group present in carboxylic acids is the ____ group.
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group –COOH.

questions.prompt: The functional group present in esters is the ____ group.
questions.explanation: Esters have the ester group –COO– between two carbon groups (RCOOR′).

questions.prompt: A structural formula shows how the atoms are ____ in a molecule.
questions.explanation: A structural formula shows how the atoms are joined up or arranged in a molecule or compound.

questions.prompt: A structural formula can be drawn as a displayed formula or a ____ formula.
questions.explanation: The two ways are the displayed formula and the condensed (normal) structural formula.

questions.prompt: A displayed formula shows all the bonds between atoms as individual ____.
questions.explanation: A displayed formula shows all the bonds between the atoms as individual lines.

questions.prompt: In a displayed formula a double bond is drawn as ____ lines.
questions.explanation: One line = single bond, two lines = double bond, three lines = triple bond.

questions.prompt: In a displayed formula a triple bond is drawn as ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Three lines show a triple bond (C≡C).

questions.prompt: A condensed structural formula groups the hydrogen atoms joined to the same ____ atom.
questions.explanation: In a condensed formula atoms attached to the same carbon are grouped, e.g. CH₃CH₃.

questions.prompt: The –CH₃ group is called the ____ group.
questions.explanation: –CH₃ is the methyl group and –CH₂– is the methylene group.

questions.prompt: The –CH₂– group is called the ____ group.
questions.explanation: –CH₂– is the methylene group.

questions.prompt: The stems for 1, 2, 3 and 4 carbons are meth, eth, prop and ____.
questions.explanation: Remember “Mice Eat Peanut Butter” = meth, eth, prop, but.

questions.prompt: The stem “eth” stands for ____ carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: eth = 2 carbons.

questions.prompt: The stem “non” stands for ____ carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: non = 9 carbons.

questions.prompt: The stem “meth” stands for ____ carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: meth = 1 carbon.

questions.prompt: The stem “hex” stands for ____ carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: hex = 6 carbons.

questions.prompt: The stem “hept” stands for ____ carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: hept = 7 carbons.

questions.prompt: The stem “pent” stands for ____ carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: pent = 5 carbons.

questions.prompt: Carboxylic acids have names ending in ____ acid.
questions.explanation: The final “e” of the alkane name is replaced by “oic acid”.

questions.prompt: Ester names end with ____.
questions.explanation: First word from the alcohol (-yl), second word from the acid (-oate).

questions.prompt: IUPAC stands for International Union of Pure and ____ Chemistry.
questions.explanation: IUPAC gives a standard set of rules for naming compounds.

questions.prompt: Every organic name is made of a stem and a ____.
questions.explanation: The stem shows the number of carbons; the suffix shows the family.

questions.prompt: The stem tells the number of ____ atoms in the longest chain.
questions.explanation: meth = 1, eth = 2, prop = 3, but = 4, and so on.

questions.prompt: The suffix shows the functional ____ (family) of the compound.
questions.explanation: The suffix is the ending of the name and is placed after the stem.

questions.prompt: The stem meth plus the ending -ane gives ____.
questions.explanation: The stem meth means one carbon and -ane means alkane.

questions.prompt: In alkanes all the carbon atoms are joined by ____ covalent bonds.
questions.explanation: All C–C bonds in an alkane are single bonds.

questions.prompt: The simplest alkane is ____.
questions.explanation: Methane (one carbon) is the simplest alkane.

questions.prompt: Propane has two C–C bonds and ____ C–H bonds.
questions.explanation: Propane has 2 C–C bonds and 8 C–H bonds (ten bonds in all).

questions.prompt: CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃ is the condensed formula of ____.
questions.explanation: CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃ means CH₃, three CH₂ groups, then CH₃: five carbons, so pentane.

questions.prompt: One molecule of heptane contains ____ hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: Heptane: hept = 7 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₇H₁₆).

questions.prompt: The chain is numbered from the end that gives the ____ number to the name.
questions.explanation: Number from the end nearest to the double (or triple) bond so that its number is the smaller one.

questions.prompt: CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₃ is called pent-____-ene.
questions.explanation: From the right the double bond starts at C-2; from the left it starts at C-3; the rule is to choose the smaller number.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -ane is an ____.
questions.explanation: Name endings: -ane alkane, -ene alkene, -yne alkyne, -ol alcohol, -oic acid carboxylic acid, -oate ester.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -ene is an ____.
questions.explanation: The ending -ene shows a C=C double bond.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -yne is an ____.
questions.explanation: The ending -yne shows a C≡C triple bond.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -ol is an ____.
questions.explanation: The ending -ol shows the –OH group.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -oic acid is a carboxylic ____.
questions.explanation: The ending -oic acid shows the –COOH group.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name is “alkyl … -oate” is an ____.
questions.explanation: Esters are named alkyl … -oate, e.g. methyl ethanoate.

questions.prompt: “Mice Eat Peanut Butter” stands for meth, eth, prop and ____.
questions.explanation: M-E-P-B = meth, eth, prop, but.

questions.prompt: After drawing a formula, count ____ bonds on every carbon.
questions.explanation: C = 4 lines, O = 2 lines, H = 1 line.

questions.prompt: Using the smaller-number rule, CH₃CH₂C≡CCH₃ is named ____.
questions.explanation: Number from the end that gives the smaller number: pent-2-yne (not pent-3-yne).

questions.prompt: Using the smaller-number rule, CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂ is named ____.
questions.explanation: Number from the end that gives the smaller number: but-1-ene (not but-3-ene).

questions.prompt: Using the smaller-number rule, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂OH is named ____.
questions.explanation: Number from the end that gives the smaller number: pentan-1-ol (not pentan-5-ol).

questions.prompt: Using the smaller-number rule, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH=CH₂ is named ____.
questions.explanation: Number from the end that gives the smaller number: hex-1-ene (not hex-5-ene).

questions.prompt: Using the smaller-number rule, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂C≡CH is named ____.
questions.explanation: Number from the end that gives the smaller number: hex-1-yne (not hex-5-yne).
